summary.text: Democrat Leticia Gutierrez won the election for Texas's open 9th District on November 3, 2026, defeating Alex Mealer, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new Congress convenes on January 3, 2027.

A government relations and community outreach director with a finance degree from the University of St. Thomas, she describes a long career connecting working families with elected officials and agencies, with a focus on children's health.

paragraphs.text: Leticia Gutierrez says her parents were farm laborers and that she has called the district home for 45 years; she attended Milby High School, according to her campaign website.
She earned a bachelor's degree from the University of St. Thomas, which her Candidate Connection survey lists as Finance and Economics.

Ballotpedia lists her profession as a government relations and community outreach director, and her campaign website says she works with elected officials and government agencies on behalf of her community.
Gutierrez says she has advocated for children's health for years after her son developed asthma as a child. She describes herself as a single mother of two whose oldest son serves in the U.S. Army.
She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the redrawn 9th District, according to the Associated Press as reported by FOX 26 Houston, in a multi-candidate field.
Her campaign focused on affordability and infrastructure resilience.
Gutierrez won the November 3, 2026 general election with 57.6% of the vote to Alex Mealer's 42.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
